method: AI-assisted Codex inspection of new outputs against only their supplied reviews; no judge API call and no reuse of original labels.

rubric.supported: Every material clause and qualifier is supported by the cited supplied text.
rubric.partially supported: Some material content is supported, but a clause, qualifier, or recurring/single wording is not fully supported.
rubric.unsupported: The cited text does not support the material claim.
rubric.contradicted: The supplied text directly conflicts with the claim.
rubric.unclear: The evidence is insufficient to decide confidently.

scope.omission_method: All supplied rows were screened with issue/contrast cues; candidate passages and cited multi-issue reviews were inspected semantically. This can miss important feedback expressed without those cues.

supplied_input_omissions.feedback: A bedroom TV did not work and rooms needed refreshing.
Guests described dated or unpleasant conditions and concerns about the surrounding area.
A guest heard main-road noise but still slept well, qualifying the complaint.
Several supplied reviews reported street or guest noise.
A guest reported that the apartment lacked an oven.
A guest reported a disputed pet-fee handling experience.
A guest reported excessive heat and inadequate cooling.
A cut radiator cable left the living area cold.
A guest reported inflexible check-in and check-out arrangements.
A long negative review reported a painful mattress, corridor noise, television problems, and difficulty finding the property.
The cited review also reported shared bathrooms and an inconvenient shower two flights downstairs.

limitations: The judgments are AI-assisted and were not independently human-rated.
The rerun uses the same purposive 12 listings and does not estimate population quality.
Omission screening is reproducible but can miss feedback not captured by issue or contrast cues.
